## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tissopianusayakathā* (Kv 11.1) is a debate located in the *Kathāvatthu* of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The controversy examined in this text concerns the status of latent dispositions (*anusaya*) [Waldron 2003]. According to secondary analysis, non-Theravādin interlocutors—specifically identified as the Sammatīyas and the Mahāsaṅghikas—asserted that latent dispositions are karmically indeterminate or neutral (*anusayā abyākatā*), which would permit them to coexist with skillful (*kusala*) or neutral states of consciousness (*citta*) [Waldron 2003]. Theravādin orthodoxy challenges this stance by arguing that latent dispositions are not distinct from manifest afflictions, pressing the dilemma that if dispositions were considered dissociated from consciousness, active manifest afflictions would likewise have to be dissociated from mind, an implication rejected by both disputants [Waldron 2003].
